Capital One.
What's in your wallet?
Terms of fly.
Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
A bipartisan group of senators is calling on President Trump to rescind his recent deal
with Russia on diesel fuel, as the U.S. and Iran refrain from military strikes on the
Gulf ahead of the midterm elections in three weeks.
In Paris, Barbara Sprout reports the senators called the deal with Russia a gift to an adversary.
A dozen senators, six Republicans and six Democrats, warn in a letter to the White House
that this deal will give Russian President Vladimir Putin, quote, "more fuel to finance
his war machine."
They called the deal, quote, "a betrayal of our allies."
Last week, President Trump announced that Russia would supply diesel to global markets,
including potentially the United States, in order to help tamp down high prices.
That was an about face from a sweeping sanctions package that was signed into law last month,
aimed at depleting Moscow's resources.
Barbara Sprout and Pure News, Washington.
President Trump told reporters at the White House that the U.S. has not stopped sharing
intelligence with Ukraine, but Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine received no
advance warning from its partners about Russian missile attacks that hit civilian infrastructure
in Kiev.
Zelensky says the main target was energy infrastructure.
Pope Leo has been diagnosed with lung cancer.
NPR's Lee Hale reports that the diagnosis was confirmed after Leo underwent surgery
in Rome Tuesday.
The surgery wasn't a surprise.
Pope Leo announced over the weekend that a nodule would be removed from his lung.
But after the 90-minute operation, the Vatican provided an update and a diagnosis.
Adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.
The medical team says part of the right lung was removed.
At 71, Leo is young for a pope and exercises regularly.
The Vatican has yet to announce any further treatments.
Leo will spend the rest of the week resting at the hospital.
The schedule has been cleared up of any public events until at least October 20.
Lee Hale, NPR News.
On to the AI company, Anthropic, and it's warning that we may be just months away from
artificial intelligence bots that can self-replicate and take over internet-connected devices.
NPR's John Ruach reports.
Anthropic says some large AI models can already self-replicate, and it predicts that smaller
ones could catch up by the end of the year.
That could lead to so-called "AI worms" that get into online systems like smart TVs
or other internet-enabled devices and replicate.
Data centers could also be a target.
Since there's no central on/off switch for bots like this, they could be hard to stop.
Anthropic says they could spread like "digital slime mold" expanding in a matter of days.
The warning, in a blog post, could add to concerns about control over AI as its capabilities
grow.
On a note, Anthropic is a financial supporter of NPR, John Ruach, NPR News.
This is NPR News.
A day of peaceful student protests in France ended in small scenes of violence as hooded
young people who may have come from outside the school movement faced off with riot police.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports that some commentators say the movement is waning.
TV News showed police shooting water cannons and firing tear gas to disperse the students.
Commentators said youths from the far-left Black Bloc movement had infiltrated the student
march and come out to fight with police.
The student demonstrations have largely been supported by the left, while the violence
has been condemned by the right.
For these latest protests, union members joined the students, as did yellow vest protesters,
the largely white working class movement that rose up against President Emmanuel Macron
and high gas prices in 2018.
Yellow vest protester Jerome Rodriguez says they have the same anger as the students.
"We must come together," he said, "and bring change to France."
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
Mexico's Pacific coast is being hit by deadly weather.
Officials say that Hurricane Simon and the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel have led
to six deaths after heavy rains triggered flooding and landslides.
Five others remain missing in Baja, California, where floodwaters have swept away vehicles
and damaged homes.
Forecasters at the National Hurricane Center in Miami say Simon is strengthening as it
moves parallel to the coast and is near to becoming a major hurricane again.
I'm Jyle Snyder.
This is NPR News.
This message comes from Charles Schwab, with their original podcast Choiceology.
Choiceology is a show about the psychology and economics behind people's decisions.
Download the latest episode and subscribe at Schwab.com/podcast.
